title: The Entertainer
description: Joplin's most famous rag, revived by the 1973 film The Sting: a syncopated right-hand tune over a steady left-hand oom-pah. It is the classic introduction to ragtime rhythm and to the independent, metronomic left hand every rag demands.

arrangements.label: Intermediate
arrangements.notes: Intro and the complete first strain at a relaxed tempo; the octave intro is thinned to a single line played by the right hand in bars 1-2 and handed to the left hand in bar 3, and the bass uses single notes with close E-G-C triads instead of octaves.
teachingPoints: Left hand first: bass note on the beat, triad off the beat, no accents on the triads. Loop bars 5-8 with a metronome until it is automatic.
Right hand: the D-D#-E pickup (after a 16th rest) lands on C5 with the fifth finger on the downbeat; keep the 1-5 frame for the syncopated C E C E C, where the C5s fall every three 16ths.
Bars 13-14 (A G F# A C E, E D C A D) shift the hand up: thumb on F#4, then 3-4-5 on A-C-E.
Hold the long D5 in bars 14-15 for its full value while the left hand keeps moving through D7 to G7.

arrangements.label: Advanced
arrangements.notes: Intro and first strain in Joplin's own texture: both hands in octaves for the three-octave descending introduction, and an octave-bass stride left hand (C2-C3 / G2-G3) under the single-line melody.
teachingPoints: Intro octaves: play each D-E-C / A-B-G group as one wrist gesture; practise the hand shift down an octave between bars without looking.
Stride bass: octaves on the beat with 5-1, triads off the beat with 3-2-1; the jump from C2-C3 to the E3-G3-C4 chord must be silent and even.
Keep Joplin's marking in mind: not fast. The syncopated C5 tied across the barline (bars 5-6, 7-8) must not rush.
Bars 13-16: the melody climbs to E5 then hangs on D5 over D7 to G7; let the left hand carry the pulse through the held note.
